newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco imposes control on banana imports.
newsitem.headline: Morocco imposes control on banana imports.

text.p: Morocco has imposed temporary controls on banana imports, in a move aimed at protecting local farmers, an official at the trade ministry said on Thursday.
The regulatory bureau Office des Changes issued a circular to intermediary banks telling them to submit a prior demand for banana imports, effective from November 12, 1997, it said.
"The new circular, which is a temporary decision, will avoid threats of bankruptcy faced by banana-growing farmers," the official said.
Morocco has gradually liberalised commodity imports, including fruit, from May 1996.
Moroccan traders imported in recent months an estimated 400 tonnes of banana, mainly from Costa Rica and other Carribean countries, officials said.
The average price on the domestic market is 12 dirhams ($1.4) per kg.
The country's commodity imports excluding cereals were estimated at $253.3 million in the first half of 1996, the Office des Changes said.
